title: The Phillips Collection: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works gather diners, travellers, performers and neighbours, with quieter intervals between them.
introduction: Renoir's boating party contains several conversations, not one event commanding everyone at the table. That dispersed attention is worth carrying into the other pictures here. Daumier's sculptors concentrate on a shared object; Lawrence's travellers move towards named destinations; a clown prepares for an audience that is not yet present. The reasons people gather are different, and the paintings make those differences visible. Between these groups, landscapes and still lifes change the pace. A candle, river ice or a palm frond can organise a picture without a human exchange at its centre. This selection follows such shifts across works in Washington's Phillips Collection.
visitNote: Check the Phillips Collection’s current object pages for loans and rotations. The Migration Series entry is panel 1 of Lawrence’s sixty-panel sequence. The Phillips owns the odd-numbered panels; MoMA holds the even-numbered panels, so this single entry should not be read as the whole series.

books.title: Impressionism: A Centenary Exhibition
books.author: Anne Dayez, Michel Hoog and Charles S. Moffett
books.note: The Metropolitan Museum’s catalogue provides historical context for Renoir and Manet. It is particularly helpful for comparing the social settings of Luncheon of the Boating Party and The Spanish Ballet without treating their very different painted surfaces as interchangeable.

works.title: Luncheon of the Boating Party
works.catalogueTitle: The Luncheon of the Boating Party
works.credit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir. The Luncheon of the Boating Party. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Bottles, glasses and fruit fill a table around which attention travels in several directions. Renoir connects the diners through overlapping bodies and glances without making them respond to the same incident. The awning gathers their different conversations under one cover. Apparent informality depends on this firm arrangement: the group can remain coherent while individual people drink, talk or attend to someone outside the nearest exchange.

works.title: The Migration Series, Panel 1
works.catalogueTitle: The Migration of the Negro, Panel 1
works.credit: Jacob Lawrence. The Migration of the Negro, Panel 1. Image: WikiArt. Copyright protected (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Chicago, New York and St. Louis appear above a crowd pressing towards departure. The signs give direction to bodies simplified into dark shapes and bright clothing. Lawrence opens his sixty-panel account of African American migration from the South with collective movement, rather than the biography of one traveller. The named cities make this more than a general image of a crowd: geography becomes part of its organisation.

works.title: The Palm
works.credit: Pierre Bonnard. The Palm. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pierre-bonnard/the-palm-1926
works.description: Spreading fronds interrupt a view of buildings and vegetation. Bonnard lets the near plant take up space that a more orderly landscape might leave open for distant scenery. Colour overlaps rather than dividing the view into clean stages, and the small foreground figure gives only a partial measure of scale. Finding distance here means working around the palm, not looking through a convenient gap left for us.

works.title: The Spanish Ballet
works.credit: Édouard Manet. The spanish ballet. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/edouard-manet/the-spanish-ballet-1862
works.description: Pale skirts catch the light among costumed performers in a dim setting. Their different poses retain suggestions of movement without combining into a single dance step. Manet brings the company together through those scattered light areas, allowing individuals to remain separate within a public identity. The performance is present in costume and posture even where the group appears momentarily suspended between actions.

works.title: Woman in Profile: Madame Tennent
works.catalogueTitle: Woman in Profile (Portrait of Madame Tennent)
works.credit: Chaim Soutine. Woman in Profile (Portrait of Madame Tennent). WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/chaim-soutine/woman-in-profile-portrait-of-madame-tennent
works.description: The sharp turn of the head gives this portrait its immediate direction. Warm patches describe the face against dark clothes and a roughly handled background. Soutine's uneven surface does not dissolve the sitter into paint: the profile remains specific enough to hold its place. The comparison is between a recognisable pose and marks that refuse the smoothness we might expect from a finished likeness.

works.title: The Pink Candle
works.credit: Henri Rousseau. The Pink Candle. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: A candle, bottle, plate and fruit occupy a shallow setting, each object held by a firm outline. Rousseau makes them easy to identify but harder to place in a smoothly measurable space. Their separateness matters as much as the arrangement they form together. The plain background leaves little else to consider, so differences of height, colour and boundary give modest household things an unusually insistent presence.

works.title: The Goatherd of Genzano
works.credit: The goatherd of Genzano. WikiArt; Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The goatherd and animals establish a small, inhabited scale on the path below distant buildings. Corot's light connects the foreground to the town, while trees and rough ground frame the opening between them. No dramatic encounter is needed to explain why the figures belong here. Their ordinary passage helps join near and far, giving the landscape a use without turning it into the illustration of an incident.

works.title: Two Sculptors
works.credit: Honoré Daumier. Two Sculptors. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Two men incline towards a small sculpted form, their faces and the object emerging from a dark interior. Daumier makes their converging poses the clearest evidence of a shared task. They are looking rather than visibly working with tools, yet the attention is itself part of making. The sculpture occupies the space between them as something to judge, giving their proximity a practical reason.

works.title: Footsteps
works.credit: Kenzo Okada. Footsteps. Image: WikiArt. Copyright protected (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Scattered marks and subdued geometric areas occupy a pale field. Okada's title suggests passage through a place, though the surface supplies neither a continuous path nor a figure walking it. The intervals become important: a viewer can connect separated marks without finding a complete landscape. That bodily association is a possibility offered by the title, not a key that explains every shape.

works.title: Self-Portrait
works.credit: Piet Mondrian. Self Portrait. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/piet-mondrian/self-portrait-1900
works.description: Mondrian's bearded face looks directly outward above an open collar, modelled in warm light against a dark reddish ground. This early painting need not be treated as a puzzle containing his later grids in disguise. Its decisions concern a particular face, tonal transitions and the encounter established by a gaze. Letting it remain a portrait makes the distance from his better-known abstraction clearer, not less interesting.

works.title: Clown Making Up
works.credit: John Sloan. Clown Making Up. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/john-french-sloan/clown-making-up-1909
works.description: A performer sits at a small table beside curtains, with light concentrated on the face and preparations. Sloan places the clown before the public appearance, when costume and makeup are still things to be worked on. The figure's concentration belongs to that practical task rather than a joke. Separating preparation from performance allows the person doing the work to remain visible beneath the role.

works.title: Moonlit Cove
works.credit: Albert Pinkham Ryder. Moonlit Cove. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The moon appears between long clouds, and its reflection marks a narrow opening through dark water. Ryder withholds the detailed coastline that might locate the cove precisely. Large dark masses give the small areas of light their force, making visibility itself the subject of comparison. The reflected path draws the eye without supplying a route anyone could actually follow across the water.

works.title: Ice in the River
works.medium: Oil on canvas mounted on wood panel
works.credit: Ernest Lawson. Ice in the River. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/ernest-lawson/ice-in-the-river-1907
works.description: Broken ice, water and winter banks share a close range of pale colours. Lawson's varied strokes distinguish their surfaces without separating them into sharply outlined compartments. Buildings beyond the river prevent the scene from becoming an uninhabited winter wilderness. The surface is changing within a place people use; the dark accents and scattered trees help measure that expanse of unstable, partly frozen water.

works.title: Approaching Storm
works.credit: Ernest Lawson. Approaching Storm. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Dark clouds gather above hills, a house and water, but light still reaches sections of the ground. Lawson makes the unevenness of those conditions matter. A uniformly dark landscape would show less of the change announced by the title. Here the remaining bright passages give the approaching weather something to alter, letting one view contain both the present illumination and the threat to it.

works.title: Carcassonne
works.credit: Walter Griffin. Carcassonne. Image credit: Walter Griffin (1861 - 1935)  (American) Details on Google Art Project; Source credit: ZgFuuMNTGlhcsw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Fortified buildings rise beyond a tree-lined wall, yet Griffin does not reserve a separate, polished manner for the architecture. Broken colour describes stone, foliage and open ground alike. The town's recognisable outline survives within that shared handling. Its monumental character depends on its forms and position, while the active painted surface keeps it exposed to the same light as the less imposing growth nearby.

works.title: The Tambourine
works.credit: Jerome Myers. The Tambourine. Image credit: Jerome Myers; Source credit: 7wHjwDKUfWrLaA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Children gather beneath buildings and shopfronts that greatly exceed their scale. Pale dresses and small gestures separate them from darker walls. Myers makes the street both a built enclosure and a place temporarily occupied by play. The group is uneven, leaving room for individual movements; the architecture supplies a common measure without determining exactly how each child uses the space below it.

works.title: Evening on the Pier
works.credit: Jerome Myers. Evening on the Pier. Image credit: Jerome Myers; Source credit: ZAEVkDDWFhD1mA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Women and children sit or stand close together beside the water, while distant structures stretch along the horizon. Myers gives their gathering several degrees of rest rather than one defining event. The open distance contrasts with the bodies' proximity. A public place becomes briefly particular through the ways people occupy it, and the warm evening light connects their separate positions without making them a single conversation.

works.title: The Evangelist
works.credit: Robert Spencer. The Evangelist. Image credit: Robert Spencer; Source credit: fwHnMEF7DE48JQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The speaker's raised position gives him a clear advantage in visibility over the street crowd. Below, differences in faces, hats and posture prevent the listeners from becoming one repeated shape. Spencer organises public address through unequal heights, but that arrangement cannot tell us that every person agrees or even listens in the same way. The gathering is visible; its collective response remains less certain.

works.title: The Auction
works.credit: Robert Spencer. The Auction. Image credit: Robert Spencer; Source credit: bAHfxH45l2plVg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: People cluster at an open doorway, their attention drawn towards objects and a raised figure. Pale walls and shutters give the gathering a firm architectural frame. Spencer turns a domestic threshold into a place of public valuation: looking and waiting become parts of an exchange. The crowd's shared direction is clear, even though the painting does not require us to know what each person would pay.

works.title: After the Ride
works.catalogueTitle: After the Ride aka Visiting Neighbors
works.credit: Julian Alden Weir. After the Ride aka Visiting Neighbors. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The saddled horse identifies an activity that has paused, while the woman stands beside it beneath trees. Its darker body gives her pale dress a clear neighbour. Weir distributes dappled light across figure and ground, keeping the portrait within its outdoor setting. The title supplies an earlier action, but the picture concentrates on the quieter arrangement left after movement has stopped.

closingSections.title: Compare the reasons for gathering
paragraphs: Renoir's diners, Daumier's sculptors and Spencer's auction crowd all share a space, but they share attention differently. Returning to those differences is more useful than treating every group as a picture of sociability. This independent selection does not promise that the works are displayed together or currently available to view. Consult the collection's current records when planning a visit.
